Wai Wai NuHuman rights activist and lawyer

Born 1987 · Buthidaung, Rakhine State

Human rightsLawPolitics

A Rohingya human rights activist and lawyer from Buthidaung, known for her advocacy for democracy, women's rights and justice in Myanmar. Arrested with her family at 18 while a law student, she spent nearly seven years in Insein Prison before her release in 2012, then founded the Women's Peace Network (Arakan) and Justice for Women and has spoken at the United Nations and other international forums. She has been listed in BBC 100 Women and named a TIME Next Generation Leader.

Her story

From political prisoner to global advocate

Wai Wai Nu is a Rohingya human rights activist and lawyer known for her advocacy for democracy, women’s rights, and justice in Myanmar. She was born in 1987 in Buthidaung, Rakhine State, to Rohingya parents. Her father, U Kyaw Min, was elected as a Member of Parliament in the 1990 election as a candidate of the National League for Democracy (NLD), but the military junta refused to recognize the results. She later moved to Yangon with her family and began studying law at the University of East Yangon at age 16.

In 2005, when she was 18 and in her second year of law school, Wai Wai Nu and most of her family were arrested. She was sentenced to 17 years in Insein Prison, while her father received a long sentence in solitary confinement. She spent nearly seven years in prison, where she later said she learned deeply from the experiences of other female detainees. In January 2012, her family was released under a presidential amnesty.

After her release, she completed her law degree and began human rights work. She founded Women’s Peace Network (Arakan) and Justice for Women, focusing on women’s rights, legal aid, and peaceful coexistence among communities. She has spoken at the United Nations and other international forums on human rights in Myanmar. In 2018, she earned a Master of Laws (LL.M.) from the University of California, Berkeley.

She has received international recognition, including being listed in BBC 100 Women and named a TIME Next Generation Leader. Wai Wai Nu is widely known as a Rohingya voice for human rights and justice, and her journey from political prisoner to global advocate has made her a notable figure in Rohingya activism.
